reason: Attacked and it held. Wording: two independent pages that quote Kahn by number give the line letter for letter, including the unusual double 'other and still other', and both tie Kahn's fragment L to Diels and Kranz B12: bryankam.com/p/a-river-of-difference (which lists Kahn, The Art and Thought of Heraclitus, as its source) and a second discussion of Heraclitean flux. No drift found. Attribution: this is the strong case rather than the weak one, because the famous English tag 'you cannot step twice into the same river' is Plato's and Plutarch's paraphrase (DK B91, B49a), while B12, preserved through Arius Didymus citing Cleanthes, is the sentence editors accept as Heraclitus' own words. So the proposal has picked the genuine fragment and refused the famous misquotation, which is the opposite of the failure this month is guarding against. Scope: philosophy, pre-1999, no scripture, no content warning. Checks: node shipped.js returns shipped [] and near [] for both this wording and for the 'you cannot step twice' paraphrase, Heraclitus at 0 for the year, not banned. Format: source line leads with the name, 96 characters, no dash, no straight quote, ends in a full stop, prose kept as prose, tag Philosophy is the form of the work. Two residual quibbles, neither fatal: 'Fragments' is a collection label rather than a work title, since Heraclitus' book is conventionally On Nature, and the source names Kahn twice. The betterCitation fixes both by naming Kahn's edition as the work. Not refuted.
